newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to privatise 91 firms by mid-1998.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to privatise 91 firms by mid-1998.

text.p: The Egyptian government plans to sell some or most of the shares in 91 state companies by the end of June 1998 in an accelerated drive towards privatisation, official sources said on Thursday.
Shares in 27 of the companies will go on sale to the public through the stock exchange and for the other 64 companies the state will seek an anchor investor, they said.
The privatisation programme started in 1993 but did not start to gather pace until early this year, when a new cabinet took office under Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri.
In May, for the first time, the government sold a majority stake in a state company through the stock exchange.

The new programme is roughly in line with plans announced by Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid in September. He said then that the state would sell two companies a week for the rest of this year and three a fortnight throughout 1997.
But the government's first attempts to find anchor investors have taken longer than expected.

Obeid said on Wednesday that the state had finally agreed to sell 75 percent of the country's only brewer, al-Ahram Beverages, to an unidentified consortium at 74 pounds a share or a total of 275 million pounds ($81 million).
The state sold 25 percent of the company in July at 67 pounds a share, he added.
The privatisation programme has been in a lull for several weeks as the stock exchange adjusts to a new dealing system.

But Obeid, quoted in the government newspaper al-Ahram, said that by the end of the month the state would offer for sale 40 percent of General Silos and Storage and 2.2 million shares in Heliopolis Housing and Development. The newspaper gave no other details of these offers.
